transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Linda Kenyon.
Chipmaker NVIDIA has named its chief financial officer,
Colette Kress, as interim CEO.
This follows the resignation of CEO Jensen Wong after reports
of extramarital affairs, including
with an alleged Chinese spy.
NPR's Shannon Bond has the story.
Colette Kress has worked at NVIDIA since 2013.
She helped oversee its transformation
from a video game chipmaker to arguably the central player
in the artificial intelligence industry
and one of the world's most valuable companies.
In a statement on Thursday, she said she is, quote,
"committed to building
on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created."
Jensen Wong's sudden departure has put a spotlight
on the company's lack of succession planning.
NVIDIA's board says it's launching a search
for a permanent CEO and will consider internal
and external candidates.
Shannon Bond, NPR News.
>> Democrat Scott Colombe has defeated Mississippi Republican
Senator Cindy Hyde Smith in the U.S. Senate race in Mississippi.
Colombe's victory increases the number
of black senators to a new high.
NPR's Hansi Lo Wang reports.
>> The Democratic blue wave of the midterms has lifted the
number of black senators in the new Congress
to a historic high of seven,
includes Illinois's Lieutenant Governor Julianna Stratton
and Scott Colombe, who's said to become the first black senator
from Mississippi since Reconstruction.
On the other side of Capitol Hill,
an NPR analysis finds the new Congress is set
to include 60 black members of the House of Representatives,
as down from 63 currently, and just one away
from the record loss of four black representatives
around the end of Reconstruction.
Retirements and runs for higher office contributed
to this year's losses.
Another factor was Republican-led redistricting
that eliminated some black-represented districts
in Texas, Florida, and Louisiana,
but higher black voter turnout helped black Democrats defend a
House seat in Alabama and win more seats in North Carolina.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
>> White House envoy is Jared Kushner
and Steve Witkoff are heading to Ireland to meet
with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky
after wrapping up talks in Moscow
with Russian President Volodymyr Putin.
NPR's Charles Maynes in Moscow says the talks are aimed
at ending Russia's war against Ukraine.
>> In these conversations, it's something Ukraine's also been
after, security guarantees
against any future Russian incursion,
although we don't have details.
What we do know is that going into these talks,
U.S. officials were exploring Article 5-like guarantees
for Ukraine from the U.S. That's a reference
to NATO's collective security defense,
which if it happened would be a huge deal.
The catch, Moscow has already rejected the idea
of a NATO-lite-like status for Ukraine,
just as it rejects Ukraine's full membership in the alliance.
>> Previous discussions with mediators were held just days ago
in Abu Dhabi.
The government suspected of killing a man
at a busy Washington, D.C. gym this morning before fleeing
and shooting four more people has been identified
as a medical doctor who had been locked in a dispute
with building management over mold in his penthouse.
You're listening to NPR.
The Kennedy Center says it plans to move ticketing
over to Ticketmaster.
An NPR investigation has found
that the center's former president, Richard Grinnell,
was a paid board member of Ticketmaster's parent company
at the time of the negotiations.
NPR's Anastasia Stilkes reports.
>> Richard Grinnell was appointed
as the Kennedy Center's president in February 2025,
just as President Trump became the institution's chairman.
A few months later, Grinnell was appointed to the board
of Ticketmaster's parent company, Live Nation,
for which he was paid over $260,000.
Critics say this raises conflict of interest concerns.
Both Ticketmaster and the Kennedy Center say their
discussions predated Grinnell's dual appointments,
but current and former senior Kennedy Center staffers
who asked for anonymity due to fears of retribution say
Ticketmaster was never under serious consideration
by senior staff until Grinnell's tenure.
The Kennedy Center's main theaters remain closed.
The annual Kennedy Center honors are scheduled
to take place December 7th at Washington's Capital One Arena.
Anastasia Stilkes, NPR News.
>> Christie's in New York is due to auction off a collection
of paintings depicting the American West
from Ted Turner's Montana Ranch.
The sale will be on January 20th, with the proceeds going
to the Turner Foundation for its conservation work.
The paintings depict the grandeur of America's West.
Ted Turner founded CNN.
He died in May.
On Wall Street at last check,
the Dow was down just over 27 points.
I'm Lindy Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.
>> Oh, Kevin, it feels good to be back.
>> It sure does, Casey, and what a time the world is talking
about AI and what's going on in Silicon Valley.
And we are here with a new show to tell you all about it.
>> That's right, Kevin.
On our new show, Machine Gods, twice a week,
we'll be bringing you the biggest news in tech
and bring you unmatched access
to the real titans of this industry.
>> You can find Machine Gods from NPR on the NPR app
or wherever you get your podcasts.

topics.text: NVIDIA names CFO Colette Kress interim CEO after Jensen Huang resigns amid affair reports
Democrat Scott Colombe defeats Senator Cindy Hyde Smith in Mississippi, lifting Senate black members to seven
NPR analysis finds Congress's black House members falling from 63 to 60 in new session
Witkoff and Kushner heading to Ireland to meet Zelensky after Moscow talks with Putin
Doctor suspected of killing man at Washington gym, then shooting four more, identified
Kennedy Center to move ticketing to Ticketmaster; former president Grinnell was Live Nation board member
Christie's to auction American West paintings from Ted Turner's Montana ranch January 20
Dow closes down about 27 points at last check
